name: Hungarian nationalism
summary: Hungarian nationalism defines the nation by language, culture and a shared historical fate, from the nineteenth-century language revival and the 1848 revolution to the grievance over the 1920 Treaty of Trianon. Its current mainstream is Fidesz-era national conservatism: Christian cultural heritage, the traditional family, higher birth rates over immigration, national sovereignty against Brussels, and state backing for Hungarians living in neighbouring countries.
scope: The profile represents the mainstream contemporary national-conservative strand as set out in the 2011 Fundamental Law and Viktor Orbán's governments (2010 onward), with the older tradition of language revival, 1848 and Trianon as background. It excludes the interwar Arrow Cross and other fascist movements and the radical-right fringe (Jobbik in its early form, Our Homeland Movement), whose answers would be more ethnic and revisionist.

sources.usedFor: Marriage and family amendments, the debt rule, gender amendment and the Sovereignty Protection Office.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Hungary keeps a national health insurance system and Fidesz governments have not sought to dismantle it; adherents mostly accept state provision, though healthcare is not a core nationalist demand.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Orbán governments raised the minimum wage repeatedly as part of a work-based economy, but the sources do not tie nationalism itself to a substantial rise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Orbán-era policy mixes market tax cuts (flat tax) with state intervention in banks, energy and retail, so adherents are split rather than committed to market superiority.

public-ownership.rationale: Fidesz re-nationalised some utilities and capped household energy prices, yet also relies on friendly private owners; the position is pragmatic, not doctrinal.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Orbán government introduced a 16 percent flat income tax and family tax breaks rather than steeper rates on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Fidesz-era labour law has been criticised as weakening unions, and nationalism emphasises national unity over class organisation; inferred rather than documented.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Fundamental Law recognises property and inheritance with full compensation for expropriation, but adds that property entails social responsibility, so the right is strong but not absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Orbán's governments imposed special taxes on banks, telecoms and foreign-owned retail, framing multinationals as a threat to national economic interests.

cut-welfare.rationale: The state encourages childbearing with family benefits, though Fidesz favours work-based rather than unconditional welfare; cutting welfare as such is not an adherent position.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the national-conservative programme points to worker ownership; it favours a national bourgeoisie, so inferred opposition.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Fidesz governments tightened security and counter-terror powers after 2015 migration crisis; the link to nationalism is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Orbán-era Hungary keeps strict drug laws and its Christian-conservative outlook rejects legalisation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Hungary retains hate-speech provisions, yet Fidesz presents itself as defender of free speech against liberal censorship; adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Orbán's centralised style and supermajority rule bypassing gridlock are defended by adherents as effective, though the ideology is not formally Führerprinzip.

state-harmful.rationale: The Fundamental Law treats the state as a framework for the nation and tasks it with protecting family, language and nationhood, so anarchism is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Hungary has strict gun laws that nationalists have not campaigned to loosen; inferred from policy continuity.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Fundamental Law makes national defence a duty of all citizens and Fidesz governments expanded military spending and border police.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Christian-conservative morality opposes legalisation, though no source addresses it directly.

decide-locally.rationale: Fidesz recentralised education, local finance and municipal powers after 2010, favouring national over local decision-making.

rehabilitation.rationale: Fidesz introduced tougher sentencing (three-strikes law), so a punishment emphasis is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Article L of the Fundamental Law protects marriage as the union of a man and a woman and calls the family the basis of the nation's survival.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Article L defines marriage as the union of a man and a woman, and the 2020 amendment defines family as a father who is a man and a mother who is a woman, effectively barring same-sex adoption.

abortion-legal.rationale: The Fundamental Law protects life from conception, though Fidesz has not repealed the existing abortion law, so opposition is moderate.

more-religion-public.rationale: The preamble recognises Christianity's role in preserving the nation, though church and state are formally separate under Article VII.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Hungarian nationalism's historical grievance is Trianon rather than racial redress; Orbán has rejected race-conscious politics, so inferred opposition.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The 2025 amendment states people are male or female and Orbán opposes gender ideology, so adherents reject the claim that gender is mainly social.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Fundamental Law's National Avowal and Article H commit the state to protect Hungarian language, culture and nationhood.

gradual-change.rationale: National conservatism values continuity with the Holy Crown tradition, though Orbán's own reforms were rapid; adherents lean traditionalist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Orbán built the Serbian border fence in 2015 and opposed EU migrant quotas, saying Hungary does not want to be a diverse country.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Orbán opposes EU federalisation and mandatory EU migrant quotas, insisting on national sovereignty.

free-trade.rationale: Orbán criticises globalism and multinationals and pursues economic patriotism, though Hungary's export model depends on open trade.

nation-first.rationale: Orbán's governments explicitly put national interest ahead of Brussels and global bodies, as in refusing EU migration rules.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Orbán opposes Western interventionism and refused to back Ukraine militarily; humanitarian war runs against his sovereignty emphasis.

open-borders.rationale: Orbán fortified the southern border and treats open borders as a threat to national identity.

limit-growth.rationale: Fidesz favours industrial growth, including battery plants, and blamed the EU Green Deal for energy costs.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Orbán blamed the EU Green Deal for energy price spikes and resists costly climate mandates.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented nationalist doctrine on technology; adherents split between modernisers and traditionalists.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The Paks II nuclear expansion with Rosatom is a flagship Orbán energy project.

revolution-justified.rationale: The 1848 revolution and 1956 uprising are national symbols, but adherents today stress order; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Orbán's populist framing opposes technocratic elites and appeals to the people's will, as in national consultations.

central-planning.rationale: Hungarian nationalism strongly identifies with anticommunism and the post-1989 market system.

socialized-markets.rationale: Fidesz favours private national capital rather than public or worker ownership; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Fidesz tax policy is flat income tax and family credits; a single land tax is not part of it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hungary has no inheritance tax on close relatives and the constitution protects inheritance, which adherents defend as family continuity.

basic-income.rationale: Fidesz's work-based state rejects unconditional income, saying welfare should be earned.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Orbán favours economic patriotism but Hungary is an EU member without independent tariffs; adherents split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Orbán government directs subsidies to strategic sectors and champions national firms in banking, energy and media.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Article P calls farmland and natural resources common national heritage and Fidesz restricts land sales to protect small farmers; the link is partly inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marxist abolition of money is the opposite of Hungary's market-based national-conservatism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Fundamental Law enshrines the forint and a national central bank, so abolition is rejected.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Fidesz favours tripartite consultation but nothing like state-set wages and prices; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Fidesz rules through elections while claiming a mandate; one-party rule is not its doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Holy Crown doctrine honours the historical monarchy and Horthy ruled as regent, but modern adherents accept the republic; split.

democracy-best.rationale: Orbán calls his system an illiberal democracy and values majority will over liberal limits, so unconditional commitment is doubtful.

direct-votes.rationale: Orbán uses national consultations and referendums, as on the 2016 quota vote, to claim popular mandate.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power belongs to the Marxist tradition that Hungarian nationalists oppose.

right-to-secede.rationale: Trianon is viewed as a national injury from the loss of territory, so regions' right to leave the state is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: The nobility's historic leadership role is part of the national tradition, but modern adherents appeal to popular mandate.

political-violence-never.rationale: 1848 and 1956 are celebrated armed struggles, yet current nationalists operate by parliamentary means.

war-builds-character.rationale: Interwar irredentism led to catastrophe and modern Fidesz presents itself as pro-peace on Ukraine.

separate-church-state.rationale: The constitution says the state and churches operate separately but cooperate, and it affirms Christianity's national role, so strict separation is not the aim.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law is rooted in Christian heritage but explicitly not scripture; Article VII keeps state and church separate.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state's duty to protect nation and citizens is central; privatised justice is alien to the programme.

military-superiority.rationale: Hungary invests in defence modernisation but is a small state; superiority over rivals is not an aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Hungarian nationalism defines the nation by language and descent, including Hungarians abroad, though the constitution treats nationalities as part of the political community.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalists see the nation and its struggles, such as Trianon, as history's main frame, rejecting Marxist class analysis.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Fidesz stresses work and merit and rejects egalitarian outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not an issue in Hungary; nationalism's own land claims are historical and state-based, so inferred mild opposition.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Hungary lacks an overseas colonial legacy and Orbán has opposed reparations-style politics.

civilizational-union.rationale: Orbán promotes Christian-civilisation solidarity with Central Europe, though not formal political union.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Article O and XXXI make responsibility for self and community and a duty to defend the country part of the constitutional order, and the National Avowal stresses obligations to the nation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Article P calls natural resources a common national heritage, but the sources give no stance on intrinsic value; split.

limit-population.rationale: The state encourages childbearing under the Fundamental Law, and Orbán frames demographic decline as the national problem.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Fidesz pursues industrial growth and rejects civilisational pessimism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: National conservatism values established institutions over disruption; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Christian-conservative outlook and traditional anthropology make enhancement questionable; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; leader-centred, people-centred politics suggests scepticism of algorithmic rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No documented position; security-oriented government but also anti-surveillance rhetoric against Western tech; split.

restore-past-order.rationale: The National Avowal reconnects with the Holy Crown and pre-1944 continuity, positing a lost constitutional tradition, though Orbán claims modernity.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Orbán proclaims pragmatic results-based governance while pursuing a distinct ideological project; split.

direct-action.rationale: Fidesz works through elections and state power; direct action is not its stated strategy.

means-match-ends.rationale: No documented doctrine on this question.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A hunter-gatherer return contradicts national development and modernity goals.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The idea belongs to Marxist and utopian thought and has no place in Hungarian nationalism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The work-based state stresses reward for work over need.

production-for-use.rationale: Fidesz defends private enterprise and profit within national capital.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory is rejected by Fidesz as part of its anticommunism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Hungarian nationalism arose against Habsburg rule and was reinforced by opposition to the 1919 and post-1948 communist regimes.

collective-farming.rationale: The memory of communist collectivisation drives support for private small farmers.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not part of nationalist analysis, which blames treaties like Trianon rather than capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Fidesz cut taxes and presents itself as low-tax but also funds family policy; adherents reject taxation as theft but favour lower taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Orbán's illiberal state restricts conduct to protect Christian and family values, such as the child-protection law.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Article D and the avowal recognise collective rights of Hungarian communities abroad and national community as a rights holder.

conscription.rationale: Article XXXI allows men to be required to serve in national crisis, and adherents accept a duty to defend the nation.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The ideology values rootedness to nation and rejects exit-based libertarian logic.

state-as-business.rationale: Orbán does talk of work-based state efficiency but treats citizens as members of a national community, not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The government mixes social supports with work conditions; no stated stance on this philosophical question.

media-academia-power.rationale: Orbán attacks liberal elites in media and universities, and Fidesz closed the Central European University's operation in Budapest.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Orbán in 2022 said he meant cultural, not racial, mixing, and mainstream Fidesz avoids racial-genetic claims; fringe groups differ.

organic-representation.rationale: The Holy Crown doctrine implies estates, but modern Hungarian nationalism uses party-based representation; split.

total-state.rationale: The Fundamental Law establishes rule of law, private property and freedom of religion, so a total state is rejected.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalists from the language revival to Fidesz speak of national renewal after Trianon, communism and decline, though this is not an explicit radical rebirth doctrine.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nationalists want minority protection and symbolic recognition of Greater Hungary, but government policy rejects formal border change.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern Hungarian nationalism rests on a constitution and national sovereignty, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom was abolished in 1848, a nationalist achievement, and the Fundamental Law guarantees freedom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Fidesz rejects postmodern critique and gender studies as ideological, claiming objective truths of tradition.

universal-morality.rationale: The Christian heritage points to universal moral truths while civilisational particularism points to distinctiveness; split.

single-common-good.rationale: The National Avowal speaks of common good and national unity but gives no explicit reasoning claim.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Orbán is friendly to Israel, but the nationalist tradition includes the Arrow Cross and other antisemitic movements, so adherents are split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The 2010 citizenship law lets ethnic Hungarians abroad obtain citizenship without residence.

revive-national-language.rationale: Hungarian language revival happened in the 1790s-1840s; today it is a living language and the statement is about reviving a lost one, so neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not part of Fidesz doctrine, which favours employer-led business.

school-vouchers.rationale: Fidesz centralised and nationalised school systems and favours state-run education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Fundamental Law sets a debt ceiling of 50 percent of GDP and Fidesz stresses budgetary discipline.

economic-freedom.rationale: Fidesz combines pro-business taxes with state-directed capitalism, so the claim is not endorsed outright.

national-self-determination.rationale: Hungarian nationalism began as a drive for self-government against Habsburg rule, and the 1867 Compromise gave the nation equal status.

force-without-un.rationale: Orbán condemned Russia's 2008 Georgia invasion but opposes Western unilateral interventionism and emphasises caution about war.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The National Avowal invokes God and Christianity rather than rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Fidesz limits benefits to citizens and ties them to work, and rejects migrants' claims on welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Orbán declared a work-based society in 2014 where benefits depend on work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism stresses national unity over class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The language and cultural revival is at the heart of Hungarian nationalism, so sacrificing heritage is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Orbán sometimes presents Hungary as defying Western powers, and ties to Russia and China, but this is not a formal front; split.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Fundamental Law defines parents as father and mother, with pronatalist family framing; adherents accept distinct roles in family more than law distinguishing public roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Orbán attacks banks and foreign lenders but the national model relies on credit and the forint system, so a ban on interest is not part of it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Orbán denies racist aims, and law prohibits discrimination; segregation law is outside mainstream.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This is a Marxist claim that adherents reject.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Orbán relies on Russian oil and gas and criticises Green Deal, so adherents favour keeping fossil fuels.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Orbán says Hungary does not want to be a diverse country, expecting newcomers to adopt Hungarian and Christian culture; mostly he opposes immigration outright.

elite-replacement.rationale: In 2022 Orbán promoted the Great Replacement theory and Fidesz campaigned against Soros and Brussels for promoting migration.

proportional-representation.rationale: Fidesz changed the electoral system in 2011 to favour winners through single-member districts.

national-mission.rationale: Hungarian tradition has notions of defending Christian Europe, but spreading its government is not a goal.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Fidesz rejects gender ideology and structural patriarchy claims.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Fidesz campaigns against out-of-touch liberal and Brussels elites, while critics say it is itself corrupt; adherents agree about opponents.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is outside the mainstream and incompatible with Christian-family emphasis.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Fundamental Law's wording on 1944 occupation drew criticism over responsibility; adherents split on accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Fundamental Law gives the state wide duties to protect family, culture and the national community.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Orbán in 2022 spoke against a mixed-race Europe but later said he meant cultural; mainstream adherents do not formally call for racial discouragement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution affirms human dignity and equality before the law, though nationalist emphasis on national community qualifies it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist theory is not part of the ideology, which rejects socialism entirely.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed by Hungarian nationalists; Orbán rejects Western colonial-guilt framings.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Hungary has a single civil law; separate religious codes are not part of the tradition.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article VII guarantees freedom of religion, including change of religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Hungarian cuisine and agriculture use beef and no nationalist source proposes such a ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Article VII separates state and churches but allows cooperation on community goals, so religious instruction in state schools is compatible; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Orbán grounds legitimacy in electoral mandates and national consultation, although he curbs checks on his power.

trade-surplus.rationale: Hungary's export-led model and economic-patriotism favours trade surpluses; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Hungary's Trianon experience of expulsions makes forced removal unattractive; the ideology demands minority protection for Hungarians, though post-1945 expulsion of Germans was accepted.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: No doctrinal stance; the tradition recognises just wars of defence.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nationalism sees peoples as competitors, but Christian cooperation tempers it; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Orbán's government has broad legal tools but has not banned parties; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Orbán speaks of freedom from foreign domination (Brussels) but the republican concept is not documented.

separated-powers.rationale: The Orbán government is criticised for weakening judicial independence, and Orbán rejects liberal checks as dogma.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist vanguard party is communist doctrine, rejected by Hungarian nationalism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Fidesz favours rewards for work and the middle class over a priority to the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Hungary privatised council housing in the 1990s and Fidesz favours home ownership; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Fidesz introduced a minimum service law restricting strikes in 2010, criticised by unions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The government treats population decline as the problem, not growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Orbán has said Hungary does not want to be a diverse country, arguing diversity weakens cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is unrelated to Hungarian practice and leader-led politics.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Orbán governed under emergency decrees during the pandemic and migration crisis, with adherents defending this.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Orbán's governments capped utility prices and set price limits on staples during 2022-23 inflation.

party-controls-media.rationale: Fidesz allies built a media empire, but adherents deny government control as such; inferred from documented media concentration.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Fundamental Law places the army under constitutional state command, not party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Orbán's restrictive immigration stance implies long residence requirements, while ethnic Hungarians get fast-track citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not a Fidesz position; MPs earn well above the average.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Fidesz is highly disciplined but this is not stated doctrine.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Orbán opposes federal European integration, with sovereignty a core theme, though Article E permits limited joint exercise as EU member.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Hungary's president is commander-in-chief nominally; adherents are indifferent.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hungarian Christianity is multi-denominational and the nationalist programme has no stance on church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Article VII separates church and state, so clergy do not rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalism is patriotic and rejects revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Fidesz's child-protection law restricts LGBT content, but broad censorship is not stated; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Orbán served repeated terms and Hungary's parliamentary system has no limit for prime ministers.

recall-officials.rationale: Not part of Fidesz practice or ideology.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Hungary remains in NATO, though Orbán is a critic of NATO's role in Ukraine.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No such proposal in Hungary; markets exist.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Fundamental Law prescribes volunteer reserves, not a replacement of the army by the armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Nationalist romanticism praises the countryside and the peasant as repositories of the nation; inferred from the Populist writers tradition.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Orbán campaigns against liberal intellectual elites, though university graduates also back Fidesz.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Orbán defends Christian Europe against other civilisations and rejects multiculturalism as relativism.

death-penalty.rationale: Orbán said in 2015 the death penalty should be debated but Hungary has not restored it; adherents split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Fidesz restricts sex education on LGBT topics and bans gender studies.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Hungarian Christian conservatism has not pushed creationism, and Fidesz has not mandated it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Fidesz's child-protection law restricts content for minors, an inference for general pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Article G makes children of citizens citizens at birth, and the 2010 law extends citizenship to descendants of Hungarians abroad.

minority-language-support.rationale: Article XXIX lets nationalities use and be educated in their language, while Hungarians demand the same abroad.

religious-exemptions.rationale: No documented position; religion is protected by Article VII but exemptions are unaddressed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: National-conservatism values custom over eccentricity; inferred from Mill being a liberal.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Orbán paid off the IMF loan early in 2013 as a sovereignty symbol, indicating a rejection of the debt-cancellation idea.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Orbán stresses economic independence from foreign capital but without a systemic overhaul.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Fidesz passed the 2011 constitution through its own supermajority, not a constituent assembly; split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Orbán cited China and Singapore as successful non-liberal models in 2014, so adherents are open to this.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Orbán prefers helping people in place (Hungary Helps) rather than large aid and migration.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Hungary has no nuclear arms and relies on NATO; no such demand.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Fundamental Law has the National Assembly elect the president, and Fidesz preserved that.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Orbán brought the central bank under government influence after 2013; the Fundamental Law enshrines the forint.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Hungarian nationalism regards Trianon as an injury, supporting a strong claim to the historic homeland.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article XIII says property entails social responsibility and Article P treats resources as national heritage.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists condemn the Soviet system as tyranny without this doctrinal label.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Fidesz resists EU environmental regulation, indicating scepticism.

collective-defense.rationale: Hungary is a NATO member, though Orbán has been cautious about NATO activism.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Nationalists view Trianon-lost territory as injustice, though Orbán has been cautious on Crimea.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Fundamental Law maintains church autonomy, and Fidesz supports Christian churches with funding.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The president under the Fundamental Law represents national unity and should stand above party politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Because loss of territory is a trauma, adherents accept force to keep the state's integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; Hungary demands autonomy for Hungarians abroad but the model is not documented.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Holy Crown is sacred, but a sacred ruler of divine descent is not Hungarian practice.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Orbán introduced a 16 percent flat tax in 2012 and still defends it.

character-from-environment.rationale: No stance; Hungarian nationalism stresses both inherited identity and upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Fundamental Law establishes constitutional rule; adherents claim Hungary's Holy Crown tradition of constitutionalism.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Hungarian historical constitution included Crown, nobles and estates, but today's adherents do not discuss mixed government.

leader-cult.rationale: Orbán has a personalised style but there is no mass cult of statues; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Fidesz stresses motherhood and fatherhood but has not spoken on shared custody.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine rejected by Hungarian nationalists.

land-redistribution.rationale: The constitution protects property, and nationalists remember communist land seizures.

refugee-return.rationale: Hungarian nationalists support the right of ethnic Hungarians expelled or displaced to return, a persistent minority-rights demand.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism seeks at least Hungarian-populated areas beyond borders, though the government avoids formal claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Freedom of religion is guaranteed by Article VII.

women-must-cover.rationale: No such demand in Hungarian nationalism.

common-currency.rationale: The Fundamental Law enshrines the forint and Fidesz has rejected adopting the euro.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Turanism has historically claimed kinship with Turkic peoples, but Orbán's Organization of Turkic States ties are cultural, not union; split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Article D commits Hungary to support collective rights and self-government of Hungarian communities abroad.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Article D tells communities abroad to keep identity and rights in their home countries, though Jewish statehood differs.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalists see ethnic nations and ideas as the movers of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Orbán attacks multinational monopolies but also favours national champions.

no-bailouts.rationale: Orbán let banks fail in certain cases but also supports national firms with aid; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Orbán's illiberal state rejects liberal limits on majority rule, and Fidesz changed judicial structures.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Fidesz opposes quotas and has few women ministers.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Hungary's export model and EU membership prevent an autarkic bloc, though economic patriotism is stressed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Fidesz resists EU green and labour mandates.

moral-incentives.rationale: The work-based state uses material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: A Guevarist approach is not part of the Hungarian tradition.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Titles were abolished in 1947; modern nationalists do not seek restoration nor oppose it.

public-money-creation.rationale: Orbán's central bank policy is orthodox with some state influence, not full public money creation.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The National Avowal frames Hungary's history around the nation and Orbán's curriculum put Hungarian history at the centre.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hungary has no colonial tradition and Orbán opposes Western interference in others' affairs.

patriotic-education.rationale: Fidesz's national curriculum emphasises patriotic education and national symbols.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Orbán rejects race-conscious politics, supporting colour-blind admission and hiring.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nationalism stresses duty to the national community over self-interest, though Fidesz also rewards personal enterprise; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine that Hungarian nationalists oppose as part of their anticommunism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Interwar revisionism sought this outright, and today the state supports unity of the nation across borders by cultural and civic means rather than border change.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Orbán's governments cultivate cultural, economic and political influence in the Carpathian Basin among Hungarian communities in former Kingdom territories.

delink-world-market.rationale: Hungary's growth depends on export links, so delinking is not an adherent view; the question concerns poor countries, hence an inference.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not used by Hungarian nationalists.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Fidesz regulates private conduct on family and cultural grounds, but anti-discrimination law exists; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Fundamental Law has an entrenched rights chapter amended by two-thirds, but Orbán's rejection of liberal limits qualifies support; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Trianon is seen as a dictated treaty dividing a people without consultation, a view adherents apply to their case; inferred beyond the colonial context.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Fundamental Law makes modern Hungary a republic with elected governments, and the Holy Crown tradition included elected kings.

minority-veto.rationale: The majoritarian style of Fidesz rejects minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Golden Bull of 1222 had a right of resistance and 1848 was a stand against absolutist Habsburg violation of the constitution; part of the national tradition.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The National Assembly is the principal lawmaking body, and Fidesz uses its two-thirds majority to legislate.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Hungary has animal-welfare laws and traditional farming, with no sign of nationalist objection; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Hungarian tradition of Széchenyi and the gentry's service to nation implies duty of the privileged; Fidesz favours patriotic business owners.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Hungarian nationalism calls for civic engagement in the nation's cause.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Orbán criticises liberal media but has not adopted the Frankfurt School view; split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian analysis not drawn on by nationalists, though they criticise liberal cultural hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Orbán complains multinationals take profits out of Hungary, a partial echo; split.

native-born-offices.rationale: Article G and nationalism favour citizens; this question's strict native-born rule is not documented.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-party question outside the programme.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Orbán's early IMF loan repayment symbolised self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revisionism defined interwar policy, but modern Fidesz avoids official claims while allowing symbolic Greater Hungary references, so split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not an issue for Hungary; inferred opposition to ethnic-priority claims from outside Hungarian context.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fidesz frames the constitution around anticommunism and rejects the leftist antifascism tradition.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Fundamental Law preamble denies legal continuity with communist rule and treats Nazi and Soviet occupations as parallel tyrannies.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Fidesz defends national historical figures such as Horthy-era memory, and monuments of the national past.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Hungary resisted ratifying the Istanbul Convention but no documented stance on symmetry.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Orbán described his model as an illiberal state in his 2014 Băile Tușnad speech, breaking with liberal dogma and implying Western forms are not universal.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The constitution puts the army under civilian control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Fidesz pays childcare benefits and lifetime income tax exemption for mothers of several children.

filial-duty.rationale: Article XVI says adult children must care for needy parents.

office-by-exam.rationale: No documented stance; Hungary has civil-service rules but the ideology doesn't address it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Orbán has used economic patriotism to restrict foreign ownership and invested in national owners.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Hungarian law already allows no-fault divorce and Fidesz hasn't changed it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Fidesz operates with strong party leadership and no imperative mandate.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Orbán's 2010-11 government nationalised the private pension funds, bringing them back into the state system.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Article P treats farmland as national heritage but does not abolish private ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Fundamental Law requires a budget law and sets dissolution if it is not approved.

single-official-language.rationale: Article H makes Hungarian the official language, though Article XXIX allows nationalities to use theirs; Hungarians abroad demand more.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Hungary restricts foreign purchase of agricultural land, a flagship Fidesz policy on a constitutional basis.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Conservative nationalism criticises consumer culture, but this isn't documented.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Orbán refused to send arms to Ukraine.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Hungary was subject to the 1956 Soviet intervention, so adherents reject such interventions.

corporate-influence.rationale: Orbán attacks multinational and global capital influence.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Fidesz built a Sovereignty Protection Office to guard national "constitutional identity" against outside influence, and Orbán frames foreign-funded influence as a threat; the NGO funding law itself is not described in the pages opened.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Fundamental Law commits the state to encourage childbearing and Fidesz gives tax breaks and loans for children.

residents-only-property.rationale: Hungarian law restricts land buying by non-locals and foreigners, a related policy.

job-guarantee.rationale: Orbán's public works scheme provides jobs but the state is not a general guarantor.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Fundamental Law ties citizens to national duties and the rule of law.

non-intervention.rationale: Orbán insists on non-interference by Brussels in internal matters and extends the principle abroad.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed in nationalist sources, so adherents are indifferent.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Fidesz campaigns portrayed George Soros and a network as conspiring against the nation, though framed as political rather than ethnic by adherents.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Article L protects marriage as a union of man and woman and the base of the nation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Fundamental Law guarantees access to public data but Fidesz is criticised for limiting it.

local-production.rationale: Fidesz champions Hungarian food and local producers, in line with economic patriotism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Hungarian nationalism operates through parties and the state.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Orbán's government invoked constitutional identity in defiance of EU rulings and the Fundamental Law says Hungary's constitution prevails.

religious-nation.rationale: The National Avowal sees Christianity as preserving the nation but treats nationalities and varied religions as part of the community; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Hungarian nationalism arose in opposition to subordination to Vienna and Moscow.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The statement describes communism; adherents reject common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The anticommunist stance is central to post-1989 Hungarian nationalism, but its mandate for 'defeat' is rhetorical today.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Fidesz uses church and private providers in schools and health alongside state, so inferred acceptance.

religion-illusion.rationale: The National Avowal affirms Christianity's role in preserving the nation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Fidesz champions national capitalism, though critical of liberal globalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Fidesz favours family policy over systemic change for women.

socialized-care.rationale: The Fundamental Law makes family primary and parents responsible for raising children.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Article H protects the Hungarian language, but language purism of the 19th-century reformers is not a modern aim.

majority-settlement.rationale: Hungarian nationalism condemned Romanian and Slovak settlement of Hungarian regions; adherents avoid such tools themselves.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The populist writers' third-way tradition has echoes, and Orbán speaks of a work-based state outside both liberal and socialist models.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Hungarian irredentism rests on the historical Kingdom of Hungary and the Holy Crown lands.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream Fidesz condemns the Holocaust though denial exists on the fringe.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Homosexuality is legal in Hungary, with restrictions on marriage and adoption, which adherents defend.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Fidesz wins elections, though critics accuse it of pressure on opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Article VII protects freedom of religion, and the state treats religious communities separately.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Hungary lacked overseas colonies; inferred rejection.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not applicable to a Christian nationalist ideology.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The constitution is secular, and adherents accept legal order.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Orbán uses national consultations and referendums but not workplace participation; split.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The Fundamental Law was amended in 2025 to say Hungarians are male or female, and Orbán backed laws restricting LGBTQ rights; legal recognition of gender identity is opposed.

assisted-dying.rationale: The Fundamental Law protects human life and Christian conservative opinion opposes euthanasia.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Fidesz claims to represent the nation rather than a left or right, but identifies itself with the right; split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist concept not used by nationalists.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Orbán has described Muslim migrants as a threat to Christian European culture, though he rejects calling Islam hostile in general.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The preamble refers to God and the Holy Crown as embodying statehood, but the constitution roots power in the people; split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not a documented controversy in Hungary.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The sources do not discuss workplace nondisclosure rules, so no position can be inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Orbán embraces market economy with family support, though prefers 'work-based' labels.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Article XXXI requires national defence and a reserve system.

rich-first.rationale: Fidesz favours building a national bourgeoisie that others follow; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Hungary is in NATO but Orbán balances between East and West; split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hungary is a republic and adherents don't favour hereditary succession of the head of state.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nothing in the sources suggests user-owned credit banks; Fidesz favours national private and state-influenced banks, so mild opposition is inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Orbán opposes outside conditions on national policy and sees sovereignty as paramount against bodies like the EU; the early IMF repayment is not documented in the pages opened, so this is inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The Fundamental Law grants universal suffrage.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept not used by nationalists.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Orbán accuses liberal media of bias and elites of power but does not adopt a class analysis.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Fundamental Law is built on rule of law with promulgated statutes, though critics charge selective implementation.

racial-franchise.rationale: Voting is universal for Hungarian citizens, with nationality rights for minorities; this is not racial.

online-participation.rationale: Fidesz's national consultations include online forms but no principled stance.

open-government-data.rationale: The constitution guarantees data access, though practice is criticised.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Article VII protects religion and Hungary has civil marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream Fidesz condemns antisemitic acts and boycotts, although fringes differ.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Fidesz prefers referendums and national consultations to sortition assemblies.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Orbán criticises global capital but supports national oligarchy; split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The government resists LGBT recognition in public institutions.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Communist-era atheist promotion is remembered as oppression.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Hungary demands collective rights and self-government for Hungarians in divided societies abroad, inferred to power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Fidesz supports churches' charity but keeps state support; split.

term-limits.rationale: Orbán has no limit on prime ministerial terms and defended continuity.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Demographic decline and migration are the stated existential issues rather than extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Hungary's Catholic and Calvinist traditions generally restrict some offices; no direct stance.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Fidesz stresses mother and father roles but not hierarchical authority; split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Orbán opposes extending political rights to foreigners.

rent-control.rationale: Fidesz favours home ownership, and no rent caps were enacted.

abolish-ip.rationale: Hungary protects intellectual property and Fidesz favours property rights.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Interwar movements used uniformed youth (Levente) and Jobbik's Magyar Gárda was uniformed, but mainstream Fidesz does not; split.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Hungary hosts none and no one proposes them; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Hungary is a NATO member with allied presence; split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Hungary recognises some genocides but the question is general; weakly inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Orbán's work-based state ideal says income should come from work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nationalism supports defence of the nation and its citizens.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The National Avowal traces the nation to St Stephen and beyond, with continuity of the Holy Crown.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The 2025 amendment declares Hungarians to be either male or female, a rejection of constructionist accounts of sex.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: 1848 and 1956 martyrs are central to commemoration, though 'saints' language is not national doctrine.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Orbán frames politics as civilisational clash but not formally spiritual; split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Article D commits Hungary to responsibility for Hungarians abroad and cultural ties.

culture-before-state.rationale: The language revival preceded the state in the 19th century, but Fidesz uses state power for culture; split.

god-not-male.rationale: Hungarian Christianity traditionally uses male terms; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Orbán's economic patriotism favours Hungarian-owned firms in banking, retail and media over foreign ones.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Hungarians abroad seek territorial autonomy for Hungarian-majority areas, e.g. Székely Land, which Hungary supports.

independent-unions.rationale: No stated stance; Fidesz-era labour law shows tension.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The statement belongs to socialist debates.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Orbán re-nationalised utilities and capped prices, with state and municipal ownership of essentials.

second-chamber.rationale: Hungary's unicameral parliament since 1945 is accepted by Fidesz but the historical Upper House of the Kingdom lives in tradition; split.

family-wage.rationale: Fidesz's family policy supports families through tax and wage measures, and the constitution calls family the nation's basis; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Regulatory speed for drugs is not addressed in nationalist sources, so adherents are indifferent.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is not part of the national-conservative programme, so adherents are indifferent.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Fidesz governments favour tracking for tax compliance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Orbán's governments have pressed for platform regulation; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: The constitution's dignity clause sets human dignity first but the nation community has priority; split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The National Avowal's appeal to God and Christianity reflects a spiritual view of human beings.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Fidesz curtailed municipal powers and favours unitary state.

gm-crops.rationale: Fidesz defends traditional agriculture and resists EU regulatory mandates; opposition to GM crops is inferred from this rather than documented in the pages opened.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; rural romanticism suggests mild opposition.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Orbán frames politics by nation and civilisation, not race, though fringe groups differ.

racial-pride.rationale: Orbán opposes treating one's heritage with shame, though his framing is national and cultural.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Hungary's modern posture and Orbán's peace line on Ukraine support defensive use.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Hungarian nationalism began with the language revival, defining the nation through Hungarian language and culture.

communal-electorates.rationale: Hungary has a common electoral roll, with nationality list for minorities.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Trianon is remembered as the work of the great powers dismembering Hungary, a persistent theme.

free-public-college.rationale: Hungary offers state-funded places alongside fees, and Fidesz has not taken a stance.

future-generations.rationale: The National Avowal pledges responsibility to descendants and the Fundamental Law covers care for natural heritage.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Fidesz's emphasis on motherhood implies complementary values.

arms-reduction.rationale: The sources show no position; Hungary expanded defence spending, but this is not tied to a stated doctrine, so neutral.

open-diplomacy.rationale: No stance; Orbán's diplomacy is often private.

capital-controls.rationale: Orbán has used taxes on foreign banks but not capital controls; split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Orbán's government banned militias like the Magyar Gárda in 2009 and 2013.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The constitution makes defence a citizen duty.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Fidesz-era reforms weakened collective bargaining while retaining tripartite forums; split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Fidesz's family tax allowances support working families.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The Fundamental Law pushes public debt below 50 percent of GDP, restricts the Constitutional Court on budget matters until then, and lets the president dissolve parliament over an unapproved budget.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Orbán criticises global order but offers no developing-world programme; split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Fidesz uses state power instead of destroying it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Orbán favours a national model, not communities choosing.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Article P treats natural resources as national heritage, not capital; split.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; Hungary's student loan system is state-run with Fidesz modifications.

sacred-nation.rationale: The preamble describes the nation as a community given spiritual meaning by the Holy Crown and past generations.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Fundamental Law's affirmation of inviolable human dignity and Christian heritage suggests a common human nature, but Orbán sceptical of redesign.

public-service-media.rationale: Critics note Orbán's government placed public media under its influence, so adherents don't treat independence as a principle.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Fundamental Law roots the nation in Christianity and its heritage, so a syncretist view is inferred to be unwelcome.

farm-price-support.rationale: Orbán governments back domestic farmers with subsidies and land protection, though this is not a defining nationalist demand.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Hungary has none and is in NATO; the sources give no stated view.

workers-own-party.rationale: Fidesz-era nationalism presents the nation, not class, as the political unit and runs as a broad national party; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Christian-conservative, family-centred state, which does not defend the practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; Hungarian law gives equal property rights and the Fundamental Law is built on equal citizens; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The Fundamental Law treats Hungarian as one language of the nation including Hungarians abroad; inferred application to the statement.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The Orbán state is interventionist and regulatory; a tort-only model is inferred to be opposed.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Lawmaking is the parliament's under the Fundamental Law; no formal role for traditional leaders, inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not a stated position; Fidesz governments have prioritised economic growth and sovereignty, so subordinating liberty to environment is inferred to be unwelcome.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the law-and-order approach of Orbán governments, not directly sourced.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Hungarian is the official language under the Fundamental Law and governments restrict immigration; a language duty on settlers is inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the national-conservative stress on individual liberty and the Fundamental Law; the sources do not discuss union rules.

voter-id.rationale: Fidesz governments stress election integrity and require identification to vote, but the sources do not set out a stated position.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Fundamental Law gives Christianity a special role in preserving the nation, so adherents favour recognised historic churches over equality of all.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Orbán defends his governments as democratic because they won free elections while pursuing illiberal policies, so adherents tend to treat elections as sufficient.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the Christian-conservative stress on the traditional family and marriage; the sources do not address premarital sex directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the Fundamental Law's protections for expression and Fidesz's stress on sovereignty; shutdowns are not discussed in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Fidesz family policy ties support to work and children, which cuts against an unconditional cash payment replacing welfare; inferred, not stated.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Fundamental Law states that women and men have equal rights, and the Fidesz-era mainstream accepts women's vote and office-holding as settled.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the defence of Christian heritage as a pillar of the nation, so adherents would reject the claim that religion oppresses women.

race-social-construct.rationale: The nation is defined by language, culture and shared history, and adherents often treat peoples as natural units; the sources do not discuss the scientific question.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Fidesz governments oppose what they call gender ideology and favour family policy instead, so dedicated equality agencies are unlikely to be wanted; inferred.

missingStatements.text: A country's constitution should affirm its Christian heritage as part of the nation's identity.
missingStatements.rationale: The National Avowal recognises Christianity's role in preserving the nation, a defining Fundamental Law feature that existing religion statements capture only loosely.

notes: Many answers are inferred from Fidesz-era policy because the nationalist tradition has no single programme; the radical-right fringe would answer ethnic, revisionist and race statements more strongly, and interwar Horthy-era revisionism was more territorial than today's government.
